claims.text: DFT calculations can facilitate the production of noble-metal-based high-entropy alloy three-dimensional nanoframeworks with precise atomic control.
DFT can predict the most stable structures of NM-HEAs.
DFT can identify optimal synthesis conditions for NM-HEA three-dimensional nanoframeworks.
Ab initio calculations or molecular-dynamics simulations can guide the NM-HEA synthesis process.
The diverse compositions and complex surface structures of NM-HEAs can be represented through theoretical modeling.
DFT calculations enable prediction of thermodynamic properties of NM-HEAs.
DFT calculations enable prediction of kinetic properties of NM-HEAs.
Predicted thermodynamic and kinetic properties can guide the synthesis of NM-HEA three-dimensional nanoframeworks.
Using DFT guidance will increase the yield of NM-HEA three-dimensional nanoframeworks with precise atomic control by 20% relative to previous synthesis methods.
HRTEM and XRD can be used to assess the claimed yield of nanoframeworks with precise atomic control.
The targeted NM-HEA three-dimensional nanoframeworks have a diameter of 100 nm.
The targeted NM-HEA three-dimensional nanoframeworks have a surface roughness of 5 nm.
The hypothesis can be tested by comparing NM-HEA nanoframework synthesis with and without DFT guidance.
Failure to obtain at least a 15% yield increase with DFT guidance falsifies the hypothesis.
